note.p: that Sir Jno Doyley is Sir John Hadley D'Oyly, 6th Bt., (1754-1818) who was then living in Ireland; by March 1800 he was at Belvedere Place, in Dublin (B.L. Add. MS 29177, fos.220). Belvedere Place presumably refering to the Rochfort Family who were Earls of Belvedere. Sir John having married Diana Rochfort one of daughters of Sir William Rochfort. By October 1802 he was living at Wainsford House, near Rathfarnham, just outside Dublin (B.L. Add. MS 29178, fos.285-6). He was living in Ireland as he had become an anonymous partner in a brewing and distillery business with his wife's relations, two of whom were Edward and Richard Grange and are possibly two of the three Granges noted in the same entry. Sir John was a close friend of Warren Hastings (the references above relate to their correspondence), one time Governor General of India, and benefitted from his patronage whilst working for the East India Company, he later returned to the EIC when brewery enterprise failed. He was also M.P. for Ipswich from 1790 for which see the entry in the History of Parliament. that Sir Jno Doyley is Sir John Hadley D'Oyly, 6th Bt., (1754-1818) who was then living in Ireland; by March 1800 he was at Belvedere Place, in Dublin (B.L.
